reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC6810-5.1-1.note: Forbidden: accepting a Prefix PDU whose Max Length is below its Prefix Length. TestParseIPv4PrefixMaxLenLessThanPrefixLen (prefix 24, max 16, otherwise valid) fails unless parseIPv4Prefix errors with "invalid"; the check sits in parsePrefixPDU, which the IPv6 parser shares. Positive: max 24 over prefix 8 yields a VRP with MaxLength 24.

RFC6810-5.1-3.note: Receipt of unspecified-content fields proven for every router-received PDU that has one: IPv4 Prefix (TestRFC6810ReservedPrefixOctetsIgnored), IPv6 Prefix header zero field, reserved flags and zero octet all ones still authorize 2001:db8::/32, and Cache Reset octets 2-3 0xFFFF still reset (TestRTRReservedOctetsIgnoredOnReceipt). Serial Notify, Cache Response and End of Data carry Session ID there, not a reserved field. Negative: the same 0xFFFF in a Cache Response is read as Session ID.

RFC6810-6.1-1.note: Single-polarity positive (row annotation). TestRTRPollsAtLeastHourly: after an End of Data with zero interval fields, pollDelay(true) and pollDelay(false) are both at most one hour; the running cacheGroup queries again when the wait ends (Reset then Serial on the wire with a 1s wait), so the loop does re-query. TestRFC6810DefaultPollCadenceIsHourly keeps the fresh-session defaults.

RFC6810-6.3-1.note: Same units as RFC8210-8.3-1: TestRTRCacheResetReloadsTheWholeSet, one-session group, Cache Reset makes the next wire query a Reset Query and its load replaces the old set; negative: data in answer to the Serial Query keeps Serial Queries and merges.

RFC6810-6.4-1.note: Forbidden: stopping, or sending anything but a Reset Query, after No Data Available with no other cache. TestRFC6810NoDataAvailableRepeatsResetQuery runs one live cache that answers two queries with Error Report code 2 and asserts three consecutive received queries are pduResetQuery, each within 4s (t.Fatal on silence, assert.Equal on a Serial Query). Negative: once the cache supplies a load the route validates and the next query is pduSerialQuery, so the reset mode ends at the usable load.

RFC6810-7-1.note: Single-polarity positive (row annotation). Same unit as RFC8210-9-1: TestRTRUnprotectedTCPFromConfig drives a config-parsed trusted-network cache (default port 323) over plain TCP to a completed sync with the VRP used.
